A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WebAgent-R1 and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E. Corresponding material can be matched despite pagination changes and appendix-table renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original WebArena-Lite experiments with trained Qwen2.5-3B and Llama3.1-8B agents, training dynamics, ablations, and test-time scaling analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds WebVoyager out-of-distribution evaluation results in Table 4.

M1.justification: Behavior cloning, M-GRPO, binary rewards, context compression, and independent browser rollouts retain the same procedures. Renaming 'asynchronous' rollout to 'parallel' rollout and clarifying the compression template do not establish algorithmic changes.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluation on 125 WebVoyager tasks across Allrecipes, Amazon, Arxiv, Coursera, and Google Map. This extends coverage beyond the retained WebArena environment to unseen websites, including recipe, research, and education tasks.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator set in Table 2 is unchanged. The new WebVoyager comparison extends the existing Qwen2.5-3B prompting and SFT baselines to another benchmark; additional citations do not introduce evaluated competitors.

E3.justification: The added evaluation randomly samples 25 tasks per WebVoyager domain and compares Qwen2.5-3B variants without further training, reporting domain and average success rates. Existing WebArena splits, training settings, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 3.5 adds the first explicit cross-environment generalization test, assessing transfer to five unseen websites without further training. This substantially extends the questions tested; existing initialization ablations, prompting analysis, interaction-budget analysis, and appendix case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added WebVoyager table continues reporting point estimates without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports WebAgent-R1 success rates of 28%, 24%, 24%, 44%, and 40% across the five WebVoyager sites, averaging 32% versus 8.8% for prompting and 12% for SFT. These are substantial new results under a new setting. Existing WebArena-Lite results, including 33.9% and 44.8% for the proposed agents, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation, behavior-cloning objective, M-GRPO loss, importance ratios, and group-relative advantage remain mathematically unchanged. No new theoretical results, assumptions, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same framework contributions, WebArena-Lite performance claims, and findings about behavior cloning, thinking, and interaction-based scaling. The additional OOD study does not redefine these stated core contributions.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new results as evidence of OOD generalization and adds concrete limitations concerning text-only inputs, unavailable verifiable rewards, fixed action vocabularies, and destructive actions in deployment. Existing explanations of behavior cloning, long-CoT training, and learning dynamics remain intact.

D1.justification: Section 2.3 explicitly clarifies that each earlier observation is represented by a template containing only a few tokens; the 'Simplified HTML' example already existed. This is a limited documentation refinement. Appendix hardware, hyperparameters, prompts, and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds seven cited works, including SelfElicit, RAST, Spurious Rewards, TruthRL, and work on separating search from answering. These extend existing citation groups without substantially changing the paper's positioning relative to prior web-agent and multi-turn RL research.

P1.justification: V2 consistently replaces 'asynchronous' with 'parallel,' makes localized explanatory edits, and adds OOD discussion, a limitations section, and acknowledgments. The principal narrative and section organization remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds the WebVoyager results table and updates Figure 2's rollout label. Existing appendix Tables 4–6 become Tables 5–7, with modest text reflow. The other plots and appendix trajectory illustrations retain their content.

improvement.justification: The new WebVoyager evaluation provides useful evidence of transfer beyond the training environment, while the limitations section makes applicability boundaries more explicit. These strengthen the otherwise stable paper, although the added evidence covers one backbone and a 125-task subset, with sparse evaluation details and no uncertainty estimates.
